text: Welcome

This playbook is your operating manual for the CRM we set up for you. It walks through the full life of a lead: what happens automatically the moment someone submits your ad form, what you need to do when they reply, and how your updates feed directly back into better campaigns and better leads.
The system is built around one simple split. We capture the lead and start the conversation. You take it from there.

caption: The working split between Waiz and you.

text: The one rule that matters most: speed. Leads answer the person who reaches them first. Every section in this playbook exists to help you respond in minutes, not hours.
Your CRM at a glance
Everything happens in one place. On desktop, the left navigation gives you the four areas you will actually use:
Conversations – every text thread with every lead, in one inbox
Contacts – the full record for each lead: info, fields, notes, tags
Opportunities – your pipeline board, where leads move through stages
Calendars – appointments, if you book calls through the system
Get the mobile app
Download LeadConnector so you can call and text leads the moment they come in, from anywhere. Log in with the same email and password as your desktop login.
iPhone / iPad: search "Lead Connector" on the App Store
Android: search "Lead Connector" on Google Play
Turn on push notifications when the app asks. This is how you find out about a new lead within seconds.
When a new lead comes in
The moment someone submits your ad form, three things happen automatically: the contact is created in your CRM, you get a notification, and the lead lands in your pipeline under New Lead.

caption: The life of a lead: the top row is automatic, the bottom row is yours.

text: Here is what that looks like in your pipeline. The new lead appears as a card in the first column, with its source and details attached:

caption: A new lead lands in the New Lead stage of your pipeline.

text: Call within 5 minutes. Contact rates fall off a cliff after the first few minutes. When the notification hits your phone, open the contact and dial. The app makes this a two-tap motion.
How the automated follow-up works

While you are getting to the phone, the system is already working. The lead receives a first text within about five minutes of their inquiry, and a short follow-up sequence continues on schedule until they respond.
Two things make this sequence different from a generic drip:
It adapts to intent. The messaging changes based on what the lead actually expressed on the form, so the follow-up speaks to what they asked about rather than sending everyone the same script.

It speaks as your assistant. Messages are sent on behalf of your assistant, not as you. That way nothing puts words in your mouth or represents you incorrectly before you have personally spoken with the lead.

caption: The follow-up sequence in plain terms: it works until the lead replies, then hands off to you.

text: The drip has exactly one job: start the conversation. It is not a replacement for calling. The leads that turn into business are almost always the ones who got a call fast and a text fast.
When the lead responds
The moment a lead replies, two things happen automatically: the follow-up sequence stops (no double-texting, no robot talking over you), and the lead moves to the Contacted stage in your pipeline.

From this point forward, every reply is yours. Go to the Conversations tab to read and respond. Keeping replies inside the CRM keeps the entire history of the lead in one thread, on desktop and in the mobile app.

caption: The Conversations tab: your inbox for every lead. Select a thread to read the history and reply.

text: Reply fast here too. A lead who texts back is live right now. Minutes matter as much on the reply as they do on the first call.
Your pipeline
The pipeline lives under Opportunities in the left navigation. It is your at-a-glance view of where every lead stands.

text: The first two moves are automatic. Everything after that is you: as a lead heats up, cools down, or moves toward closing, drag the card to the stage that matches. Thirty seconds of pipeline hygiene per lead keeps your whole book organized.
Want more granularity? You can add your own stages under pipeline settings. Just keep the stages we set up intact: do not rename or delete them, because the automation and reporting depend on them.
Tags: the only two you need
Tags in this system are deliberately simple. You will only ever add two, and each one takes two seconds from the contact record.

caption: The two tags you own, and what each one does.

text: Add claimed whenever you have had a real conversation with a lead: a call that connected or a genuine text exchange. This is how we measure your contact rate together, and it is the single most useful signal for judging lead quality.
Add kill-switch when a contact should receive no automated messages at all: they asked to stop, they became a client, or any other reason. It shuts off everything instantly.
Deal outcomes are not tags. Proposals, submissions, funded deals, and disqualifications are all reported through the Client Log form on the next page.
The contact record: fields and notes
Select any contact to open their full record. The basics (name, phone, email, source, and their form answers) fill in automatically from the ad. Two areas are yours to maintain:
Custom fields (left panel of the contact) – update these as you learn more: timeline, amounts, qualification details. Structured data here means you never have to re-ask a question.
Notes – after every real conversation, leave a short note: what was said, any objections, and the agreed next step. Future-you will thank present-you every time a lead calls back three weeks later.
Use the fields we set up first. If you feel a field is missing, tell us before creating your own so the data stays clean and reportable.
Logging outcomes: the Client Log
This is the highest-leverage two minutes in the whole system. Every deal outcome is reported through the Client Log form. There are two event types.
Conversions

When a lead reaches Proposal, Submitted, or Funded: open the form, search the lead by name, pick the event type, and enter the loan size and date. One submit per loan; the same house with two loans is two submits.

caption: Logging a conversion: pick the lead, the event type, the loan size, and the date.

text: Disqualifications
When a lead does not qualify, log it with the reason: LTV, FICO, low property value, seasoning, low income, or other. The optional notes box is for anything that adds context.

caption: Logging a disqualification: select the reason so we know exactly what happened.

text: Why this matters so much
Your logged outcomes close the loop between your desk and your ad campaigns:
We trace every outcome back to the specific ad that produced the lead, so we can kill what produces bad leads and scale what produces good ones.
Cleaner outcome data lets us steer the campaigns toward the kinds of leads that actually turn into business for you, not just the ones that fill out forms.

caption: The feedback loop: your two minutes of logging drives the next month of lead quality.

text: If you only build one habit, make it the after-call one: note, tag, next step. Everything else in the system flows from leads being touched and recorded while the conversation is still fresh.
What not to touch
The CRM is yours to work in, but a few things under the hood keep the automation and reporting running. Please check with us before changing any of these:
Workflows and automations
Pipeline structure: the stage names and order we set up
The core tags (renaming claimed or kill-switch breaks tracking)
Lead source fields
The text templates inside the follow-up sequence
Integration settings and user permissions
Adding things is usually fine: your own pipeline stages, notes, and field updates are all encouraged. When in doubt, ask first. It takes us thirty seconds to answer and can save hours of untangling.
Quick answers
I did not get a notification for a new lead.

Check that push notifications are enabled for the LeadConnector app in your phone settings, and that you are logged in. If both look right, message us and we will check the notification settings on our side.
The automated texts kept going after the lead replied.
That should never happen. Flag it to us immediately with the lead's name and we will fix it the same day.
I cannot find a lead.
Search by name or phone number in Contacts. If you are looking at the pipeline, check whether a filter is applied at the top of the board.
Can I add my own leads to the CRM?

Yes, you can create contacts manually. Just know that manually added contacts do not enter the automated follow-up sequence unless we set that up for you. Ask us if you want your own lists worked by the system.
Something else?
Message us in your Slack channel or reach out to your client success contact. That is what we are here for.
